---
title: "clean gisaid data"
output: github_document
date: "2025-02-20"
---

## objectives

-   read in gisaid metadata for H5Nx sequences
-   parse information from genbank titles incl species, location, year
-   fill in missing metadata with parsed information
-   for species (mix of common and latin), harmonize to common names
-   remove vaccine, passaged, cloned
-   remove rows with incomplete date, country, species, no HA
-   make a unique ID complete for all (sample), remove duplicate segments within sample
-   read in gisaid sequences and separate by segment
-   exclude meta removals from seqs
-   summarize number of gisaid seqs by species/country/year, length of seqs
-   export cleaned unaligned seqs and metadata
-   read in protein sequences
-   parse protein names and match to nucleotide samples
-   remove redundant protein seqs within sample
-   summarize proteins in final data, width of data

## Changes in v2
-   incorporate change in clean_ncbi regarding hosts lookup, more efficient purrr instead of loooping lists
- protein sequence changes

```{r}
rem.vacc3<-meta$isolate_id[str_which(meta$isolate_name, "A/Vietnam/1203/2004")]

#MDCK isolate embryonated chicken egg isolate? are these considered cultured?

#Culture, clones, muts

# table(meta$passage_history)
#anything with more than one passage (might be more hiding, not sure what all the entries mean)
pass<-"P2|P3|P4|P5|P6|p2|p3|p4|p5|p6|Clone|clone|mutant|adapted|passage 2|passage 3|passage 4|passage 5|passage 6|Passage 2|Passage 3|Passage 4|Passage 5|Passage 6|2nd passage|multiple|reassortant"

# table(str_subset(meta$passage_history,pass)) %>% sort

#all removals

#REMOVE them!

    paste0("Excluded, passaged/lab derived: ",length(c(rem.passage,rem.lab))),

    file=text.out,sep="\n",append = T)
```

## Parse information from IDs
```{r warning=FALSE}
#re-wrote this parsing function with help of chatgpt to utilize purrr instead of for loops over lists, and overall more efficient/less redundant

#location lookup list
unq_loc<-unique(c(meta$country,meta$continent,meta$state,meta$city))
unq_loc<-unq_loc[unq_loc!=""]
us.states<-usa::state.name
china<-read.csv(china.cit.in)
china.region<-unique(china$admin_name)
cit<-maps::world.cities
cities<-cit$name
unq_loc<-unique(c(unq_loc,us.states,china.region,cities,"British_columbia","Guangdong-shenzhen","Hong kong"))
unq_loc<-unq_loc[unq_loc!="Turkey"]

meta$host_parse<-NA
meta$location_parse<-NA
meta$date_parse<-NA

year_range<-1905:2025
all.years<-paste(as.character(year_range),collapse="|")
abb.yr<-c(as.character(50:99), #abbr years
          paste0("0",as.character(0:9)),
          paste0("1",as.character(0:9)),
          paste0("2",as.character(0:5)))
abb.years<-paste(abb.yr,collapse="$|^")
abb.years.s<-paste0("^",abb.years,"$")
nolets<-paste(paste0(c(letters[1:26],LETTERS[1:26]),"-"),collapse="|")

parse_isolate_one<-function(t,unq_loc,all.years,abb.years.s,nolets){
  if(is.na(t)||t=="")return(list(host="",location="",date=""))
  if(str_detect(t,"gullNorway"))t<-str_replace_all(t,c("gullNorway"="gull/Norway"))
  t1<-unlist(str_split(t,"/"))
  my_n<-length(t1)
  if(my_n<2)return(list(host="",location="",date=""))
  my_host<-t1[2]%>%str_to_sentence()%>%trimws()%>%str_replace_all("R\\(","")%>%str_replace_all("_"," ")
  if(my_host=="Est"&&my_n>=4){
    my_host<-t1[4]%>%str_to_sentence()%>%trimws()%>%str_replace_all("R\\(","")%>%str_replace_all("_"," ")
  }
  if(is.na(my_host)||length(my_host)==0)my_host<-""
  if(str_detect(my_host,"Reassortant")&&my_n>=3)my_host<-last(unlist(str_split(t1[3],"\\(")))
  if(str_detect(my_host,"Hong Kong|Hong kong")&str_detect(t,"MDCK|Embryo"))my_host<-"Embryonated chicken egg"
  if(str_detect(my_host,"Influenza a virus|Influenza A virus|Puerto Rico"))my_host<-""

  my_location<-""
  if(my_n>=3)my_location<-trimws(t1[3])
  if(my_host%in%unq_loc){my_location<-my_host;my_host<-""}
  if(length(my_location)>0){
    if(my_location%in%c("chicken","duck","pigeon","Mallard","little cuckoo-dove")&&my_n>=2)my_location<-t1[my_n-1]
    if(str_detect(my_location," X | x "))my_location<-unlist(str_split(my_location," X | x "))[1]
    if(str_detect(my_location,paste(as.character(1950:2025),collapse="|"))&&my_n>=4)my_location<-last(unlist(str_split(t1[my_n-4],"\\(")))
    if(str_detect(my_location,paste(paste0("-",0:9),collapse="|")))my_location<-unlist(str_split(my_location,paste(paste0("-",0:9),collapse="|")))[1]
    if(my_location=="7732")my_location<-"Ontario"
  }
  if(length(my_location)==0||is.na(my_location))my_location<-""

  tailtok<-t1[my_n]
  t1.1<-unlist(str_split(tailtok,paste0("\\(|_|\\s+|-H5N1|\\|\\|\\||（|",nolets)))
  t1.1<-trimws(t1.1)
  t1.1<-t1.1[t1.1!=""]
  my_date<-str_subset(t1.1,all.years)
  my_date<-str_replace_all(my_date,c("2016s"="2016","20200"="2020","2021|^-2021|M2021"="2021","20222"="2022"))
  if(length(my_date)>1)my_date<-my_date[which.max(str_length(my_date))]
  if(length(my_date)<1){
    my.yr<-str_subset(t1.1,abb.years.s)
    if(length(my.yr)>1)my.yr<-my.yr[length(my.yr)]
    if(length(my.yr)==1){
      if(my.yr%in%paste0("0",as.character(0:9)))my_date<-paste0("20",my.yr)
      if(my.yr%in%paste0("1",as.character(0:9)))my_date<-paste0("20",my.yr)
      if(my.yr%in%as.character(50:99))my_date<-paste0("19",my.yr)
    }
  }
  if(length(my_date)<1||is.na(my_date))my_date<-""
  list(host=my_host,location=my_location,date=my_date)
}

parsed<-purrr::map(meta$isolate_name,~parse_isolate_one(.x,unq_loc,all.years,abb.years.s,nolets))
meta$host_parse<-vapply(parsed,`[[`,"",1)
meta$location_parse<-vapply(parsed,`[[`,"",2)
meta$date_parse<-vapply(parsed,`[[`,"",3)

```

```{r}
  meta$host[undersc]<-host.vec
}
```

## Convert remaining latin species to common
```{r latin to comm, message=F}
latinx<-c("us$|is$|is |ara$|ae$|ea$|ia$|um$|Anser|es$|yla$|ped$|vison$|iba$|aca$|ata$|tta$|ubo$|alis$|allus|vus|stela|gata|xii|xa|ax|buteo|Larus")
latinx<-unique(str_subset(meta$host,latinx))
latinx<-latinx[-str_which(latinx,c("Alpaca|Mallard|-necked ibis|-eared|Multispecies|Munia|munia|Rhea|rhea|Ibis|ibis|houbara"))]
latinx1<-unique(unlist(str_split(latinx," ")))
latin.all<-unique(c(latinx,latinx1))

latin.still<-which(meta$host%in%latin.all)
length(latin.still) #285

latin.look.df<-data.frame(latin=unique(meta$host[latin.still]),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

if(file.exists(latin.look.in)){
  latin.look.df2<-read.csv(latin.look.in, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
  latin.look.df<-latin.look.df%>%left_join(latin.look.df2,by="latin")
}
if(!file.exists(latin.look.in)){latin.look.df$common<-NA}

length(which(is.na(latin.look.df$common))) #29

need<-which(is.na(latin.look.df$common))
if(length(need)>0){
  out.list<-purrr::map(latin.look.df$latin[need],~taxize::sci2comm(.x)%>%unlist())
  out.first<-vapply(out.list,function(x){if(length(x)>0)str_to_sentence(x[1])else NA_character_},character(1))
  latin.look.df$common[need]<-out.first
}

na.comm<-which(is.na(latin.look.df$common))
length(na.comm)
latin.look.df$latin[na.comm]
#only looks latin (is common) # African houbara "Chlamydotis undulata"
#fixed as exception above
# latin.look.df$common[which(latin.look.df$latin=="African houbara")]<-"African houbara"

if(!dir.exists("lookups")){dir.create("lookups")}
write.csv(latin.look.df,"lookups/latin-common.csv",row.names=FALSE)

latin.map<-setNames(latin.look.df$common,latin.look.df$latin)
meta$host[latin.still]<-unname(latin.map[meta$host[latin.still]])

# table(meta$host)%>%sort()
length(unique(meta$host)) #612
sort(unique(meta$host))
```

## Clean up country and location
```{r}
# where is country missing where we have other location info?
nocount<-which(meta$country=="")
nocount<-which(is.na(meta$country))
# meta$location[nocount]
# meta$location_parse[nocount]
#weird ones, use the location looked up
meta$country[nocount]<-str_replace_all(meta$location_parse[nocount],
                                       c("Kagoshima"="Japan", "AB"="Canada", "RV1"="Vietnam") )
nocount<-which(is.na(meta$country))
length(nocount) #now actually complete

#check turkey country vs species
turk<-which(meta$country=="Turkey")
meta[turk,c("host","country","isolate_name")] #fine

#lookup continuent and region
dfc<-data.frame(country=unique(meta$country))
# which(is.na(dfc$country))
#we already have continent in gisaid data and it's complete/seps north and south amr
dfc$continent<-countrycode(dfc$country, origin="country.name", destination= "continent")
dfc$region<-countrycode(dfc$country, origin="country.name", destination= "region23")
#add missing
dfc[which(dfc$country%in% c("Antarctica","South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands","Torgersen Island")),
    c("region","continent")]<-"Antarctica"
#kosovo neihbours Macedonia
dfc$region[which(dfc$country=="Kosovo")]<-dfc$region[str_which(dfc$country,"Macedonia")]
dfc$continent[which(dfc$country=="Kosovo")]<-dfc$continent[str_which(dfc$country,"Macedonia")]
dfc$region<-str_replace(dfc$region,"Australia and New Zealand","Oceania")
dfc$region<-str_replace(dfc$region,"Northern America","North America")
table(dfc$continent) %>% sort
table(dfc$region) %>% sort

#new weird ones:
dfc[which(dfc$country=="French Southern Territories"),c("continent","region")]<-
  c("Antarctica","Antarctica")

dfc[which(dfc$country=="Roberts Island"),c("continent","region")]<-
  c("Antarctica","Antarctica")

dfc[which(dfc$country=="Livingston Island"),c("continent","region")]<-
  c("Antarctica","Antarctica")

#making a new global region, nearest to Africa (but not really)
dfc[which(dfc$country=="Gough_Island"),c("country","continent","region")]<-
  c("Gough Island","Africa","Southern Atlantic")

#should be no NAs
any(is.na(dfc$region)) #F
write.csv(dfc,"lookups/country_continent.csv")

dfc.less<-dfc[,c("country","region")]

## connect this back to the meta to export with data (can be used for subsampling later)
meta<-meta %>% left_join(dfc.less, by="country") #multimatch expected
```

## Make meta long (one row per segment)
```{r}
## make long
meta.long<-meta %>% pivot_longer(2:9,names_to = "segment",values_to = "segment_id")

#remove these
meta.long<-meta.long %>% select(-he_segment_id, -p3_segment_id) 

## parse out segment 
meta.long$segment<-str_replace_all(meta.long$segment, "_segment_id", "")
meta.long$segment<-str_to_upper(meta.long$segment)
#replace MP with M
meta.long$segment<-str_replace_all(meta.long$segment,"MP","M")
table(meta.long$segment)

## add a new column for nucname (isolate id date segment) for export and going forward
# isolate_id, collection_date, segment
meta.long<- meta.long %>% 
  unite(nucname, "isolate_id","collection_date","segment",sep="|", remove = F)
head(meta.long$nucname)

## add a match_name that matches to current names(nuc) elements )
meta.long<- meta.long %>% 
  unite(match_name, "isolate_id", "segment",sep="|", remove = F)
length(which(duplicated(meta.long$match_name))) #good
# meta.long$segment_id[1:100]

# meta.long<- meta.long %>% unite(nucname.n, "isolate_id","collection_date","segment",sep="/", remove = F) #03-28 fix, right order
head(meta.long$match_name)

#any duplicates?
dup<-which(duplicated(meta.long$nucname))
length(dup) #niceee

#any NA?
any(is.na(meta.long$nucname))

cat(paste0("Final nrow meta/nuc sequences gisaid: ",nrow(meta.long)),
    file=text.out,sep="\n",append = T)
```

# Connect meta and sequences, filter excluded in meta from nucs, and split by segment

## Read in the sequences and compare to meta
```{r}
#Read in the nucleotide sequence
nuc1<-Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(nuc1.in)
nuc2<-Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(nuc2.in)
nuc3<-Biostrings::readDNAStringSet(nuc3.in)
#note, ignoredinvalid one-letter sequence codes ? ambig

#Join the three fasta
nuc<-c(nuc1,nuc2,nuc3)
length(nuc) #363401
length(nuc)/nrow(meta) #average of 8.6, because this meta has excluded some 
names(nuc) %>% head() #new meta col to match

#names df to parse
names(nuc)<-str_replace_all(names(nuc), "MP","M") #this segment should just be M
nuc.names<-data.frame(seq_name=names(nuc))

## first parse concat acc/genbank title
nuc.names<-nuc.names %>%  separate(seq_name, sep = "\\|", into=c("isolate_id","segment_id1","segment_id2","segment","extra","extra2"), remove = F) #extra cols because some have more | than others... ugh

#assign the extra as segment where applicable
extra.rows<-which(nuc.names$extra2 %in% segments)
nuc.names$segment[extra.rows]<-nuc.names$extra2[extra.rows]

# extra.rows1<-which(nuc.names$extra1 %in% segments) #none here
table(nuc.names$segment) #uneven, because there are dups here that we'll have to choose between

#check if all segments check out TTT
which(!nuc.names$segment %in% segments) %>% length ==0
any(is.na(nuc.names$segment))==F
which(nuc.names$segment=="") %>% length ==0

#can all isolate ids from meta be found in the sequence data? 
all(meta$isolate_id %in% nuc.names$isolate_id) #yes
#make a match name that will be used to combine to nuc
nuc.names<-nuc.names %>% 
  unite(match_name, "isolate_id","segment", sep="|", remove = F)

#find duplicated nuc.names match_name USE BELOW
dup.nucs<-which(duplicated(nuc.names$match_name))
length(dup.nucs) #23,985. quite a bit...
length(dup.nucs) /nrow(nuc.names) *100 #6.6% of data 

cat(paste0("N sequences duplicates within isolate_id|segment: ", length(dup.nucs)),
    file=text.out, sep="\n", append = T)
```

## Deal with multiple seg_ids per isolate_id and segment

```{r}
# nuc.names[which(nuc.names$match_name==a),]

# #[1] "EPI229671|A/chicken/Yamaguchi/7/2004, EPI1063|A/chicken/Yamaguchi/7/2004"

```

## Find widest segment sequence where multiples exist
```{r}
#build stable match_ID in nuc.names (isolate_id|segment)
nuc.names$match_ID<-paste(nuc.names$isolate_id,nuc.names$segment,sep="|")

#map nuc.names seq_name to actual nuc indices and compute widths
nuc.names$nuc_idx<-match(nuc.names$seq_name,names(nuc))
nuc.names$w<-NA_integer_
ok<-which(!is.na(nuc.names$nuc_idx))
if(length(ok)>0)nuc.names$w[ok]<-Biostrings::width(nuc[nuc.names$nuc_idx[ok]])

#for each match_ID, keep the widest sequence (tie-break by first occurrence)
keep.df<-nuc.names%>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(nuc_idx))%>%
  dplyr::group_by(match_ID)%>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(w),nuc_idx,.by_group=TRUE)%>%
  dplyr::slice(1)%>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

#restrict nuc to only match_IDs present in meta.long (drop nucs removed for other reasons)
keep.df<-keep.df[keep.df$match_ID%in%meta.long$match_name,]

#filter nuc to the selected sequences and name by match_ID (stable key)
nuc.f<-nuc[keep.df$nuc_idx]
names(nuc.f)<-keep.df$match_ID

#filtered nuc.names for downstream consistency checks
nuc.names.f<-nuc.names[nuc.names$match_ID%in%names(nuc.f),]

#fill meta.long with the stable key (now seq_match_name==match_name)
meta.long$seq_match_name<-meta.long$match_name

#check for any remaining meta rows without a matched nucleotide sequence
miss<-which(is.na(meta.long$seq_match_name)|meta.long$seq_match_name==""|!meta.long$seq_match_name%in%names(nuc.f))
length(miss)

#final consistency checks between meta.long and filtered nuc
all(meta.long$seq_match_name%in%names(nuc.f))
all(names(nuc.f)%in%meta.long$seq_match_name)
```

## remove seq where meta was excluded
```{r}
#meta.long should only contain match_names present in nuc.f
meta.long<-meta.long%>%
  dplyr::filter(match_name%in%names(nuc.f))

#reorder meta.long to match nuc.f order (so downstream is consistent)
meta.long<-meta.long[match(names(nuc.f),meta.long$match_name),]
all(meta.long$match_name==names(nuc.f))

#if you still want a "nucname" column for exporting headers, set it to the stable key
if(!"nucname"%in%colnames(meta.long))meta.long$nucname<-meta.long$match_name
meta.long$nucname<-meta.long$match_name

#ensure nuc.f names are the stable keys (match_name)
names(nuc.f)<-meta.long$nucname
all(names(nuc.f)==meta.long$nucname)

#add year to collection_date (handles yyyy, yyyy-mm, yyyy-mm-dd; keeps yyyy-only as-is)
meta.long$collection_year<-str_extract(meta.long$collection_date,"^[0-9]{4}")
table(meta.long$collection_year)
```

## New seq ID 
```{r}
#Create unified sequence ID: isolate_id, date, and segment
meta.long<-unite(data=meta.long,col="seq_new",
                 isolate_id,collection_date,segment,sep="|",remove=F)

#Build stable match key (same logic used everywhere)
meta.long$match_name<-paste(meta.long$isolate_id,meta.long$segment,sep="|")
nuc.names.f$match_name<-paste(nuc.names.f$isolate_id,nuc.names.f$segment,sep="|")

#ensure nuc.names.f has nuc indices and widths (needed to pick best per match_name)
if(!"nuc_idx"%in%colnames(nuc.names.f))nuc.names.f$nuc_idx<-match(nuc.names.f$seq_name,names(nuc))
if(!"w"%in%colnames(nuc.names.f)){
  nuc.names.f$w<-NA_integer_
  ok<-which(!is.na(nuc.names.f$nuc_idx))
  if(length(ok)>0)nuc.names.f$w[ok]<-Biostrings::width(nuc[nuc.names.f$nuc_idx[ok]])
}

#collapse nuc.names.f to one row per match_name (widest; tie-break by first nuc_idx)
nuc.names.f<-nuc.names.f%>%
  dplyr::filter(match_name%in%names(nuc.f))%>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(nuc_idx))%>%
  dplyr::group_by(match_name)%>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(w),nuc_idx,.by_group=TRUE)%>%
  dplyr::slice(1)%>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

#reorder nuc.f to match nuc.names.f 1:1
nuc.f<-nuc.f[nuc.names.f$match_name]
stopifnot(length(nuc.f)==nrow(nuc.names.f))
stopifnot(all(names(nuc.f)==nuc.names.f$match_name))

#Map unified names onto nuc.names.f using match_name
mn2new<-setNames(meta.long$seq_new,meta.long$match_name)
nuc.names.f$seq_new<-unname(mn2new[nuc.names.f$match_name])

#Sanity checks: all nuc.f entries should resolve to a new name
all(names(nuc.f)%in%nuc.names.f$match_name)
any(is.na(nuc.names.f$seq_new))==F

#Rename sequences in nuc.f to unified identifiers
new2<-setNames(nuc.names.f$seq_new,nuc.names.f$match_name)
names(nuc.f)<-unname(new2[names(nuc.f)])

```



## Check re-name
```{r}
#counts must agree across objects
stopifnot(length(nuc.f)==nrow(nuc.names.f))
stopifnot(length(nuc.f)==nrow(meta.long))

#all nuc.f names should now equal seq_new values
stopifnot(all(names(nuc.f)==nuc.names.f$seq_new))

#no missing mappings
sum(is.na(nuc.names.f$seq_new)) #should be 0

#seq_new format check: isolate_id|date|segment

length(bad.format) #should be 0

#uniqueness: no duplicate sequence names

set.seed(1)

data.frame(

)
```


# Output meta and sequences by segment
## Separate into elements of lists, Export meta and nucleotide seqs by segment
```{r}
#Output meta and nucleotide sequences by segment

#initialize empty lists to store per-segment meta and sequences
meta.segs<-nuc.segs<-vector("list",length(segments))
text.temp<-""

#split meta.long and nuc.f by segment
for(i in 1:length(segments)){
  myseg<-segments[i]
  #rows of meta.long belonging to this segment
  mymet<-which(meta.long$segment==myseg)
  #subset metadata for this segment
  meta.segs[[i]]<-meta.long[mymet,]
  #subset nucleotide sequences using unified seq_new names
  nuc.segs[[i]]<-nuc.f[meta.long$seq_new[mymet]]
  #sanity check: meta rows and sequences must match 1:1
  stopifnot(nrow(meta.segs[[i]])==length(nuc.segs[[i]]))
  #append counts to text output
  text.temp<-paste0(text.temp,"\n N sequences ",myseg,": ",nrow(meta.segs[[i]]))
}

#print summary to log file
cat(text.temp,file=text.out,sep="\n",append=T)

#export per-segment metadata and nucleotide fasta files
purrr::iwalk(seq_along(segments),function(i,idx){
  write.csv(meta.segs[[i]],meta.out[i])
  Biostrings::writeXStringSet(nuc.segs[[i]],nuc.out[i])
})

```

```{r}
prot3<-Biostrings::readAAStringSet(prot3.in)
prot<-c(prot1,prot2,prot3)

length(prot) #531473
head(names(prot))
# width(prot)
```

## Parse protein names, filter dups by protein, filter no meta match (same isolate_id?)
```{r}
prot.names<-data.frame(seq_name=names(prot))

x<-stringr::str_split(prot.names$seq_name,"\\|")
prot.names$isolate_id<-purrr::map_chr(x,~.x[1])
prot.names$protein<-purrr::map_chr(x,~.x[length(.x)])

#isolate_name is usually the token right before protein (e.g., A/.../2021)
prot.names$isolate_name<-
  purrr::map_chr(x,~if(length(.x)>=3).x[length(.x)-1]else NA_character_)

#everything between isolate_id and isolate_name/protein becomes the messy protein_id_raw
prot.names$protein_id_raw<-purrr::map_chr(x,~{
  if(length(.x)<=3)return(NA_character_)
  paste(.x[2:(length(.x)-2)],collapse="|")
})

#optional: derive collection_date from isolate_name if it ends with /YYYY or /YYYY-...
prot.names$collection_date<-stringr::str_extract(prot.names$isolate_name,"[0-9]{4}(-[0-9]{2}(-[0-9]{2})?)?$")

#harmonize protein naming
prot.names$protein<-stringr::str_replace_all(prot.names$protein,c("^NS2$"="NEP"))

#deal with these sillies with improper protein naming 
ix.emb<-str_detect(tolower(prot.names$protein),
                   "publishing_embargo")
# id.emb<-which(ix.emb)
if(any(ix.emb)){
  prot.names$protein[ix.emb]<-prot.names$isolate_name[ix.emb]
}

#check
table(prot.names$protein) #niiice
# head(prot.names)

```

## Filter proteins to match meta.long and no dups
```{r}
#Filter proteins to only nucleotide-retained isolates (meta.long$isolate_id)
keep.iso<-unique(meta.long$isolate_id)
keep.row<-which(prot.names$isolate_id%in%keep.iso)
cat(paste0("protein sequences removed due to isolate_id not in nuc meta: ",
            nrow(prot.names)-length(keep.row)),
    file=text.out,sep="\n",append=T)

#filter dat
prot.names.f<-prot.names[keep.row,]
prot.f<-prot[match(prot.names.f$seq_name,names(prot))]
stopifnot(all(prot.names.f$seq_name==names(prot.f)))

#Compute amino-acid lengths for deduplication
prot.names.f$aa_len<-Biostrings::width(prot.f)

#Key for duplicate detection: isolate_id|protein
prot.names.f$iso_prot<-paste(prot.names.f$isolate_id,prot.names.f$protein,sep="|")

#Detect duplicates
dup.k<-sum(duplicated(prot.names.f$iso_prot)) #35617
cat(paste0("duplicate isolate_id|protein rows detected: ",dup.k),
    file=text.out,sep="\n",append=T)

#Deduplicate: keep widest protein per isolate_id+protein (tie-break = first)
prot.names.f<-prot.names.f%>%
  dplyr::group_by(iso_prot)%>%
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(aa_len),dplyr::row_number(),.by_group=TRUE)%>%
  dplyr::slice(1)%>%
  dplyr::ungroup()

#Subset protein sequences to match deduplicated metadata
prot.f<-prot.f[match(prot.names.f$seq_name,names(prot.f))]
stopifnot(all(prot.names.f$seq_name==names(prot.f)))

cat(paste0("protein sequences removed due to duplicate isolate_id|protein (kept widest): ",dup.k),
    file=text.out,sep="\n",append=T)
```

```{r}
  prot.f<-prot.f[-rm.M]
}
stopifnot(all(prot.names.f$seq_name==names(prot.f)))
```

##Separate proteins and their meta in list
## Rename
```{r}
#create stable protein identifier (parallel to ncbi: prot_accession|nuc_accession|protein)
prot.names.f<-prot.names.f%>%
  tidyr::unite(newname,isolate_id,protein_id_raw,protein,sep="|",remove=F)

#rename sequences to newname (keeps 1:1 order with prot.names.f)
names(prot.f)<-prot.names.f$newname
stopifnot(length(prot.f)==nrow(prot.names.f))
stopifnot(all(names(prot.f)==prot.names.f$newname))
```

## Export proteins
```{r}
prot.meta<-prot.segs<-vector("list",length(prot.ord))
text.temp<-""

for(i in 1:length(prot.ord)){
  myprot<-prot.ord[i]
  matchprot<-which(prot.names.f$protein==myprot)
  matchprotacc<-match(prot.names.f$seq_name[matchprot],names(prot))
  prot.segs[[i]]<-prot[matchprotacc]
  prot.meta[[i]]<-prot.names.f[matchprot,]
  names(prot.segs[[i]])<-prot.meta[[i]]$newname
  text.temp<-paste0(text.temp,"\nN sequences ",myprot,": ",length(prot.segs[[i]]))
}
cat(text.temp,file=text.out,sep="\n",append=T)

##Export unaligned proteins and corresponding meta
prot.ord2<-str_replace_all(prot.ord," |\\/","")
prot.meta.out<-paste0(f.out,"gisaid_protein_meta_",prot.ord2,".csv")
prot.out<-paste0(f.out,"gisaid_protein_",prot.ord2,".fasta")

purrr::iwalk(seq_along(prot.ord),function(i,idx){
  if(nrow(prot.meta[[i]])>100){
    Biostrings::writeXStringSet(prot.segs[[i]],prot.out[i])
    write.csv(prot.meta[[i]],prot.meta.out[i])
  }
})

#total final proteins
write.csv(table(prot.names.f$protein), paste0(f.out, "prot.names.f_proteins.csv"))
```
